did_you_know.text: Did you know? Josiah began to reign when he was only eight years old, and he reigned in Jerusalem for thirty-one years. His mother was Jedidah, the daughter of Adaiah, from Bozkath.

Did you know? The chapter describes Josiah as a king who did what was right in the eyes of the LORD and followed in every way the example of his ancestor David, without turning aside to the right or left.
Did you know? In the eighteenth year of his reign, Josiah sent Shaphan the secretary to the house of the LORD to manage the money that had been collected and oversee the repair of the temple.
Did you know? The money collected in the house of the LORD was handed over to the supervisors of the work, who gave it to the workers to repair and strengthen the temple.
Did you know? The workers were not required to provide a detailed account of the money entrusted to them, because the Scripture testifies that they acted faithfully.
Did you know? During the repair of the house of the LORD, Hilkiah the high priest found the Book of the Law, gave it to Shaphan the secretary, and Shaphan read it.
Did you know? When Josiah heard the words of the Book of the Law, he tore his robes—an act expressing sorrow, shock, and submission before the LORD.
Did you know? After hearing the book, Josiah sent a delegation of five men, including Hilkiah the priest, Shaphan the secretary, and other court officials, to inquire of the LORD.

Did you know? The delegation went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, who lived in Jerusalem. In this way, the chapter presents a prophetess whom the king’s messengers consulted concerning Judah.

Did you know? Huldah explained that the LORD had heard Josiah’s response because his heart was tender and he humbled himself, tore his robes, and wept. Therefore, he would not see in his lifetime the disaster that was to come upon the place.
